content.text:
I made one small print fix to `0.html`; the rest of the file held up under a line-by-line read and I left it alone. Nothing was tested in a browser — my check for an installed browser was blocked by the session's permissions, so this is a static review only.

## What I changed

In the `@media print` block, `pre` and `table` now get `overflow: visible`. Both kept `overflow-x: auto` from the screen styles, and browsers may refuse to split a scrollable box across pages. A long code block or table could therefore be clipped or pushed whole to the next page.

## What I checked and left alone

- **Heading spacing:** the rules for headings, `hgroup` and sectioning elements resolve correctly in the cases I traced (sibling sections, heading followed by a section, `header` as first child).
- **Trailing margins:** the two `:last-child` rules zero the right margins, and they correctly skip `dialog` and `[popover]`, which keeps their auto-margin centring.
- **Lists, figures, definition lists:** no conflicts found.

## Judgement calls for you

- **`table { display: block }`**: this is the only way to get horizontal scrolling without a wrapper element, but it has historically stripped table semantics for screen readers in some browsers. The alternative is wrapping each table in a scrollable `div`, which costs you the markup-free approach.
- **`h4`, `h5` and `h6` all render at 1rem bold**, so those three levels look identical. It only matters if you nest headings that deep.
- **Scrollable `pre` and `table` regions aren't keyboard-focusable in Safari.** That needs `tabindex="0"` in the markup; CSS can't fix it.
- **The title and `h1` are both `0`, and there is no meta description.** I left them because I don't know what the page is for.

If "improve" meant something else — visual design, real content, or a different structure — tell me which and I'll take it that way.
